cases.description: A well‑formed YAML schema string should be detected, converted to JSON and a JsonSchema object returned.
A JSON schema containing a $ref to an external meta‑schema should be resolved (using the default config) and a JsonSchema object returned without throwing.
Passing a null schema string should result in a NullPointerException (the method does not accept null).
An empty string does not represent a valid schema and should cause an IllegalArgumentException.
A JSON schema string with leading and trailing whitespace should be trimmed and parsed successfully, returning a JsonSchema instance.
A schema string that contains only whitespace is not a valid schema and should cause an IllegalArgumentException.
An empty JSON object is a valid schema (equivalent to "any type"); the factory should return a non‑null JsonSchema instance.
Calling getSchema(null) should immediately throw NullPointerException because the method does not accept a null argument.
An empty string does not represent a schema; the method should validate the argument and throw IllegalArgumentException.
A string that contains only whitespace is not a valid schema; the method should trim the input and, finding it empty, throw IllegalArgumentException.
The JSON string is syntactically invalid (missing closing braces). Parsing should fail and the underlying Jackson parser should throw JsonParseException.

cases.description: The YAML string contains illegal syntax (extra colon). Detection as YAML should lead to a parsing attempt that throws JsonParseException.
A $ref that is not a valid URI should cause the factory to raise a JsonSchemaException during reference resolution.
When the schema references an external URI that cannot be fetched, the loader should propagate an IOException.

group: Exception - Unsupported SpecVersion Flag in Meta‑Schema Id

cases.description: A $schema identifier that refers to an unknown draft version should cause the factory to reject the schema and throw IllegalArgumentException.
